les: Die Son se agt planete en hul bure
kaps_punt: Die Son, planeete en asteroïdes - die Son ('n ster) is in die middel van ons Sonnestelsel; daar is agt planeete (Mercurius, Venus, Aarde, Mars, Jupiter, Saturnus, Uranus en Neptunus), dwergplaneete (soos Pluto) en die asteroïde-gordel in 'n baan om die Son; elke planeet het sy eie -- kenmerke, grootte, baan en posisie met betrekking tot die Son, samestelling (rotsagtig en gas planeete) en mane (sommige het geen mane); die planeete en Asteroïdes neem verskillende tye om om die Son te wentel

items.bewering: In Graad 4 het jy geleer dat die Son 'n ster is wat in die middel van ons Sonnestelsel staan.
items.blok: Die Son en alles wat om hom wentel
items.bron: KABV Natuurwetenskappe en Tegnologie Gr 4-6, Graad 4 Kwartaal 4, 'Die Aarde en die Son' (gedrukte bl. 28): 'die Son is 'n ster in die middel van die Sonnestelsel'. NASA Sun Facts (science.nasa.gov/sun/facts): the Sun 'is the center of our solar system'.

items.bewering: Alles in die Sonnestelsel wentel om die Son. Dit sluit nie net agt planete en hulle mane in nie, maar ook dwergplanete en baie asteroïdes.
items.blok: Die Son en alles wat om hom wentel
items.bron: NASA Sun Facts: the Sun's gravity holds the solar system together; NASA What is a Planet (science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/what-is-a-planet): planets and dwarf planets orbit the Sun; NASA Asteroid Facts: asteroids revolve around the Sun. Moons orbit their planets and travel round the Sun with them, as the lesson's own Mane block says.

items.bewering: Elke planeet beweeg oor en oor in sy eie wentelbaan om die Son.
items.blok: Die Son en alles wat om hom wentel
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet, opgedateer 18 Maart 2025): each planet has its own orbital distance and period.

items.bewering: Hier volg die agt planete van die naaste aan die Son tot die verste: Mercurius, Venus, Aarde, Mars, Jupiter, Saturnus, Uranus, Neptunus.
items.blok: Die agt planete, van naby na ver
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet, distances from the Sun 57.9 / 108.2 / 149.6 / 228.0 / 778.5 / 1432 / 2867 / 4515 million km in that order; NASA Planets page: 'The first four planets from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars'; Neptune 'the eighth and most distant planet'.

items.bewering: Die vier planete van Mercurius tot Mars is die naaste aan die Son. Ons noem hulle die rotsagtige planete.
items.bron: NASA Planets page (science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets): the first four planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, 'known as terrestrial planets because they have solid surfaces'. KABV uses 'rotsagtig' for this group.

items.bewering: Elkeen het 'n harde oppervlak van rots, soos die grond onder jou voete.
items.bron: NASA Planets page: the terrestrial planets 'have solid surfaces'. Mapping checked: comparing a rocky planet's surface to the ground a learner stands on holds, because Earth is itself one of the four; it does not suggest anything false a learner would reason towards.

items.bewering: Die vier planete van Jupiter tot Neptunus is verder weg. Ons noem hulle gasplanete. Elkeen het 'n baie dik buitenste laag gas en geen harde oppervlak nie.
items.bron: NASA Planets page: 'The giant planets in the outer solar system don't have hard surfaces', with swirling gases above a core (Jupiter and Saturn gas giants, Uranus and Neptune ice giants); NASA Neptune Facts: 'Neptune does not have a solid surface', atmosphere mostly hydrogen and helium. KABV itself uses 'gas planeete' for the outer four, so the grouping matches the curriculum.

items.bewering: Jupiter is die grootste planeet
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Jupiter diameter 142 984 km and mass 1898 x 10^24 kg, largest of the eight; NASA Sun Facts calls Jupiter 'the biggest planet'.

items.bewering: en Mercurius die kleinste.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Mercury diameter 4 879 km and mass 0.330 x 10^24 kg, smallest of the eight by both measures.

items.bewering: Selfs die kleinste gasplaneet is baie groter as enige rotsagtige planeet.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: smallest giant by diameter is Neptune (49 528 km), smallest by mass Uranus (86.8 x 10^24 kg); largest rocky planet Earth (12 756 km, 5.97 x 10^24 kg). Either way the smallest giant is about four times Earth's width and about 15 times its mass.

items.bewering: Van die rotsagtige planete is die Aarde die grootste.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Earth 12 756 km against Venus 12 104 km, Mars 6 792 km, Mercury 4 879 km; Earth also the most massive of the four.

items.bewering: Maar die Son is baie groter as al agt die planete saam.
items.bron: NASA Sun Facts: the Sun 'accounts for 99.8% of our solar system's mass' and is about 10 times wider than Jupiter. By diameter too: the Sun (about 1.39 million km) is more than three times the eight planets' diameters added together (about 0.40 million km, NASA Planetary Fact Sheet).

items.bewering: Hoe verder 'n planeet van die Son af is, hoe langer is sy pad om die Son. Die planete ver weg beweeg boonop stadiger. Hulle het dus baie langer nodig om een keer om die Son te wentel.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: orbital velocity falls steadily outward (Mercury 47.4, Earth 29.8, Jupiter 13.1, Neptune 5.4 km/s) while orbital period rises (88 days to 59 800 days). A larger orbit is a longer path; both causes the lesson names are real.

items.bewering: Die Aarde wentel in een jaar een keer om die Son.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Earth orbital period 365.2 days.

items.bewering: Mercurius is die naaste aan die Son en het net omtrent drie maande nodig.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Mercury 57.9 million km from the Sun (closest), orbital period 88.0 days, about 2.9 months.

items.bewering: Neptunus is die verste en het meer as 160 van ons jare nodig vir een rondte.
items.bron: NASA Neptune Facts: 'the eighth and most distant planet', orbits the Sun 'in about 165 Earth years'; NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: 59 800 days, about 164 years.

items.bewering: Die planete ver van die Son af is baie koud
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet mean temperatures: Jupiter -110, Saturn -140, Uranus -195, Neptune -200 degrees C.

items.bewering: maar die naaste planeet is nie die warmste nie. Venus is die warmste planeet
items.bron: NASA Venus Facts (science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts): 'the hottest planet in our solar system', about 467 degrees C, 'hotter even than the innermost planet, charbroiled Mercury'; NASA Planetary Fact Sheet mean temperatures Venus 464, Mercury 167 degrees C.

items.bewering: want sy dik lug hou die Son se hitte vas.
items.bron: NASA Venus Facts: 'Its thick atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect'; NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: surface pressure 92 bar against Earth's 1. Mapping checked: 'hou die hitte vas' is the standard simplification of the greenhouse effect and does not lead a learner anywhere false.

items.bewering: Die meeste planete het mane wat om hulle wentel en saam met hulle om die Son reis.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: six of eight planets have moons (Earth 1, Mars 2, Jupiter 95, Saturn 274, Uranus 28, Neptune 16).

items.bewering: Mercurius en Venus het geen mane nie.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: 0 moons for both; NASA Venus Facts: Venus is 'one of only two planets in our solar system that doesn't have a moon' (its quasi-satellite Zoozve is an asteroid, not a moon).

items.bewering: Die Aarde het een maan, en dit is ons eie Maan.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Earth 1 moon.

items.bewering: Die vier gasplanete het elkeen baie mane.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet: Jupiter 95, Saturn 274, Uranus 28, Neptune 16; the smallest count (Neptune's 16) is still many against Earth's one.

items.bewering: Die getal mane verander soms omdat wetenskaplikes nog steeds nuwe mane vind.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (moon counts revised in its 2025 update, Saturn now 274) and NASA Neptune Facts ('16 known moons'); counts are given as known moons because discoveries continue.

items.bewering: Net soos 'n planeet is Pluto rond en wentel dit op sy eie om die Son. Tog is Pluto 'n dwergplaneet.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet, quoting IAU Resolution B5 (2006): a dwarf planet orbits the Sun, has enough mass for its gravity to make it round, has not cleared its neighbourhood and is not a satellite; Pluto is classed a dwarf planet. KABV Gr 4 note: 'Pluto is nou bekend as 'n dwergplaneet'.

items.bewering: 'n Planeet is swaar genoeg om in beheer van sy eie pad te wees. Dit het die ander groot dinge op sy pad weggevee, of dit hou hulle in toom. Pluto is te lig daarvoor.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet: IAU third criterion, the planet's gravity 'has cleared away any other objects of a similar size near its orbit'; NASA describes the test as whether a body 'sweeps up or scatters away its immediate neighbors, or holds them in stable orbits'. Mapping checked: 'weggevee, of hou hulle in toom' matches both halves of that description, and 'swaar genoeg' correctly ties the test to mass. Pluto's mass is 0.013 x 10^24 kg (NASA Planetary Fact Sheet), and Pluto does not dominate its zone.

items.bewering: Baie klein yswêreldjies beweeg steeds in dieselfde deel van die ruimte as Pluto.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet: 'numerous icy worlds orbiting the Sun in a doughnut-shaped region called the Kuiper Belt', of which Pluto is described as the biggest known.

items.bewering: 'n Planeet moet swaar genoeg wees, maar dit hoef nie 'n bepaalde grootte te hê nie.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet and the IAU Resolution B5 as reported there: the criteria refer to mass and self-gravity, and the definition sets no numerical size or mass threshold for clearing the neighbourhood.

items.bewering: Pluto is een van 'n paar dwergplanete wat wetenskaplikes ken.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet: the IAU recognises five dwarf planets, Eris, Ceres, Pluto, Haumea and Makemake, and 'there may be another 100'.

items.bewering: Asteroïdes is stukke rots of metaal wat ook om die Son wentel.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts (science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/facts): C-types clay and silicate rock, S-types silicate and nickel-iron, M-types metallic nickel-iron; asteroids 'revolve around the Sun'.

items.bewering: Hulle is almal baie kleiner as enige planeet.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts: the largest asteroid, Vesta, is about 530 km across, against the smallest planet Mercury at 4 879 km (NASA Planetary Fact Sheet); all asteroids together have less mass than Earth's Moon. Ceres (about 940 km) is now classed as a dwarf planet and is also far smaller than Mercury.

items.bewering: Die meeste van hulle beweeg in 'n wye strook tussen Mars en Jupiter. Ons noem dit die asteroïdegordel.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts: 'Most asteroids orbit our Sun between Mars and Jupiter within the main asteroid belt.'

items.bewering: Die gordel skei so die rotsagtige planete van die gasplanete.
items.bron: NASA Planets page: the terrestrial planets are the first four, ending at Mars, and the asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, the first giant planet.

items.bewering: Dit is nie 'n digte muur van klippe nie. Die gordel is meestal leë ruimte met die asteroïdes ver van mekaar af.
items.bron: NASA Goddard solar system tour, Asteroids (aeb.gsfc.nasa.gov/690/solar-system-tour/Asteroids.html): 'the main asteroid belt is still mostly empty space, and spacecraft can travel through it with almost no risk of collision'; NASA news 2000 (Cassini was the seventh craft to cross with no course corrections). Mapping of the negated comparison holds: it corrects the 'wall of rocks' picture rather than creating one.

items.bewering: Hulle het langer as Mars en korter as Jupiter nodig om een keer om die Son te wentel.
items.bron: Britannica, Asteroid: geography of the asteroid belt, gives the main belt's mean distances as about 2.06 to 3.28 AU; by Kepler's third law that is periods of about 3.0 to 5.9 years, between Mars (687 days, 1.9 years) and Jupiter (4 331 days, 11.9 years) on the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet. Scope: this holds for belt asteroids, which is what 'Hulle' refers to here (the sentence follows 'die asteroïdes' in the belt). It would not hold for every asteroid: near-Earth asteroids and Jupiter's Trojans lie outside the belt, and the block's own 'Die meeste van hulle' admits there are such asteroids.

items.bewering: ster: 'n Baie groot bal warm gas wat sy eie lig maak.
items.bron: NASA Sun Facts: the Sun is 'a hot glowing ball of hydrogen and helium', 'super-hot, electrically charged gas called plasma', about 100 times wider than Earth; a NASA heliophysics presentation (ntrs.nasa.gov 20180001759): a star produces its own light, planets and moons reflect it.

items.bewering: Sonnestelsel: Die Son saam met alles wat om hom beweeg.
items.bron: NASA Sun Facts: the Sun is the centre of the solar system and its gravity holds it together.

items.bewering: planeet: 'n Groot ronde wêreld wat op sy eie om 'n ster beweeg en swaar genoeg is om in beheer van sy eie pad te wees.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet, IAU three criteria: orbits a star (for us the Sun), massive enough to be round, has cleared its orbit. 'Groot' is a description, not a size threshold, so it does not contradict the study text's 'hoef nie 'n bepaalde grootte te hê nie'; 'op sy eie' correctly excludes moons.

items.bewering: wentelbaan: Die pad waarlangs een ding in die ruimte oor en oor om 'n ander ding beweeg.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts and Planetary Fact Sheet describe orbits as repeated paths round the Sun (elliptical orbits, orbital period); KABV Gr 4: 'die Aarde beweeg in 'n baan om die Son wat 'n wentelbaan genoem word'.

items.bewering: rotsagtige planeet: 'n Planeet wat 'n harde oppervlak van rots het.
items.bron: NASA Planets page: terrestrial planets 'have solid surfaces'.

items.bewering: gasplaneet: 'n Groot planeet met 'n baie dik buitenste laag gas en geen harde oppervlak nie.
items.bron: NASA Planets page: the giant planets 'don't have hard surfaces' and have swirling gases above a core; NASA Neptune Facts: no solid surface.

items.bewering: maan: 'n Wêreld wat om 'n groter wêreld, soos 'n planeet, beweeg en saam met hom om die Son reis.
items.bron: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet lists moons by the planet (and dwarf planet, Pluto 5) they orbit; a moon orbits its parent body while the parent orbits the Sun. 'Soos 'n planeet' rightly leaves room for moons of dwarf planets.

items.bewering: dwergplaneet: 'n Ronde wêreld wat op sy eie om die Son beweeg, maar geen planeet nie.
items.bron: NASA What is a Planet, IAU Resolution B5: a dwarf planet orbits the Sun, is round, is not a satellite, and has not cleared its neighbourhood, so is not a planet; 'planets and dwarf planets are two distinct classes of objects'.

items.bewering: asteroïde: 'n Stuk rots of metaal wat om die Son beweeg en baie kleiner as 'n planeet is.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts: rocky, mixed and metallic types; largest (Vesta) about 530 km against Mercury's 4 879 km.

items.bewering: asteroïdegordel: Die wye strook tussen Mars en Jupiter waar die meeste asteroïdes wentel.
items.bron: NASA Asteroid Facts: 'Most asteroids orbit our Sun between Mars and Jupiter within the main asteroid belt.'

opsomming: All 45 claims checked against NASA, the IAU definition as NASA reports it, Britannica and the CAPS document hold, including every superlative and comparison; the one point worth a person's eye is that the last sentence of the asteroid block (longer than Mars, shorter than Jupiter) is true only of belt asteroids, which is what its 'Hulle' refers to, so it should stay tied to the belt if that block is ever reworded.
